body:
## Move in Log-Odds Steps

A one-point score increase should have a consistent meaning even near very small and very large probabilities. Ordinary probability steps cannot do that.

Logistic regression works with odds, then takes their logarithm to make weighted effects add cleanly. Each coefficient changes these log-odds by a fixed amount.

Convert coefficients back carefully when explaining them. An effect on odds is not the same as adding that amount directly to probability.
common_mistakes: Treating the output probability as certainty.
Using the default threshold without considering error costs.
Explaining an odds change as the same-sized probability change.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Move in Log-Odds Steps” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: It is a strong, explainable baseline for binary classification.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Move in Log-Odds Steps” story, explain Logistic Regression without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
